provider: Baidu AI Studio 星河社区 (aistudio.baidu.com) — dataset + notebook storage

free_tier.stated: Two separate pools, which is the interesting part: (1) Notebook persistent workspace. Verbatim 'Notebook每个用户提供 100G 的云端持久化存储空间作为个人工作区，访问路径为 /home/aistudio/work' (100 GB per user, persisted in real time); (2) Datasets. '单个文件大小要小于50GB，一个数据集最多可上传50G数据内容' (single file under 50 GB, one dataset holds at most 50 GB of content). So 100 GB standing + 50 GB per dataset, and datasets are a separately-created object, not a folder in the workspace.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: The FAQ caps a dataset file below 50 GB and a dataset at 50 GB; the notebook preview limit is 10 MB for the .ipynb main file.

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: Notebook每个用户提供 **100G** 的云端持久化存储空间作为个人工作区，访问路径为 /home/aistudio/work/。写到该目录下的文件将被实时持久化存储. ... Data目录为非持久化目录, 在Data下进行的文件操作, 重启之后会被自动恢复. ... docker容器闲置一段时间后会被回收，并且系统为docker容器强制设置了最长有效期

egress.terms: Free for public datasets. Downloads are anonymous HTTP from Baidu's CDN with no egress line and no per-GB charge anywhere in the docs. No metered-egress surface exists because AI Studio is not a cloud-storage product with a billing meter.

interface_detail: SDK/CLI, git+LFS and the web uploader
tooling: First-party pip package aistudio-sdk: `aistudio upload --repo-type {model,dataset} --include ... --max-workers N` with a User Access Token from aistudio.baidu.com/account/accessToken. Also git+LFS, and a web uploader. Python SDK + CLI both documented. No rclone backend, no S3 API.
chaining: The FAQ shows datasets being attached to a project with an add-dataset action and files above 150 MB routed through datasets; no numerical cap on dataset count is published.
limits_note: 50 GB per file, 50 GB per dataset, 100 GB persistent workspace. Notebook main file (.ipynb) capped at 10 MB for preview purposes. Free GPU is 12 h/day with an 8-point/day sign-in economy, but compute is irrelevant here. Dataset uploads above 150 MB must go through the dataset path rather than direct project upload. No documented retention/expiry on datasets.

identity_cost.detail: email + any-phone, but the platform is China-facing and prior rounds recorded Chinese pans demanding +86 real-name verification and Alipay. Treat as country-phone until a registration attempt proves otherwise.

reliability_note: Datasets are mutable (versions exist. '生成新版本'). Notebook containers are recycled when idle and have a forced maximum lifetime, but /home/aistudio/work is described as real-time persistent, so the workspace is the durable part. Heavily China-network-oriented; download speeds from outside CN are untested here.

extras.chaining_verbatim: This is the multiplier case §1 describes: 50 GB is per DATASET, and the quota field explicitly separates the 100 GB workspace from dataset storage. N datasets x 50 GB is the intended pattern (people mount several datasets into one project simultaneously — Q21 '添加数据集' shows multiple datasets attached to a single project). 20 TiB = ~410 datasets. Whether the dataset COUNT is capped is the one number I could not establish — no page states a limit on number of datasets, and the platform's own docs describe creating datasets repeatedly as normal workflow.

extras.agent_focus: New and up-and-coming competitors to Hugging Face and ModelScope, judged on the hard test the brief sets: a credible HF competitor must permit multi-TB objects and generous per-account storage, because model weights and datasets routinely run to hundreds of GB / TiB. Split into three classes — Chinese domestic hubs (HF is blocked there, so a separate ecosystem exists), Western MLOps artifact stores (W&B/Comet/ClearML/Lightning/Deep Lake), and dataset-publishing startups (Source Cooperative, Oxen, OpenDataLab). Excluded and not re-reported: Hugging Face, ModelScope, Kaggle, Civitai, Ollama, Replicate, DagsHub, OpenML, fal.ai, Baseten, Modal.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
